name: rollback-plan
conclusion_quantitative: rollback-plan (Escalate) specifies 1 of 5 categories: 10+ validation rules; none for autonomy limits, clarification rules, approval gates, escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: rollback-plan writes deployment rollback plans: triggers, decision trees, step-by-step procedures, data considerations, verification and post-rollback actions. Its only control rules are a quality checklist the plan must pass; the rest describes the plan's content for the humans who will run it. It sets no autonomy limits, clarification rules, approval gates or rules for escalating failures.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never forbids or restricts any action of the agent on files, commands, tools or other systems, and never tells it to go ahead without asking.

clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to ask the user for missing or unclear information, or to avoid guessing.

approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to get the user's permission or confirmation before doing something.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ validation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, 1 tied to a situation, all bullet points. Before delivering a rollback plan the agent checks that triggers are measurable, any on-call engineer can run the procedure, data rollback is addressed, the known-good artifact exists, verification and communication are covered, the blast radius and durations are documented, and a backup is taken when data changes.

statements.quote: Rollback triggers are measurable with specific thresholds, not subjective
Rollback procedure can be executed by any on-call engineer, not just the deployer
Data rollback is addressed — either confirmed safe or scripted and tested
Previous known-good artifact is identified and verified to exist
Verification steps cover health, error rate, latency, and business metrics
Decision tree covers auto-rollback, manual rollback, and roll-forward scenarios
Blast radius and dependency impact are documented
Estimated rollback duration is stated for each method
Database backup is taken before deployment if data changes are involved

escalation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent what to do when something goes wrong, such as stopping or reporting an error to the user.
